signals.title: USD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Liquidity Shock
signals.text: The US Dollar is the weakest G10 currency this week, falling -1.078% on average across seven pairs as the US Treasury announces plans to double bond buybacks and boost liquidity. This fiscal shift has triggered a sharp USD sell-off, with USD/CHF falling to 0.7989 and testing its SMA200 at 0.7930. The G10 spread between CHF (the week's leader at +1.003%) and USD has widened to a critical 2.081%, marking a dominant bilateral theme. While the 375bp Fed-SNB carry advantage remains the largest in the G10 space, the liquidity-driven USD tumble is overriding carry support as VIX remains low at 14.9. A sustained break below the SMA200 at 0.7930 would signal a regime shift for the pair. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CHF; fiscal liquidity surge overrides the structural carry advantage. Catalyst: US Treasury buyback execution updates. Risk: S&P 500 reversal triggers a flight to USD liquidity, closing the G10 spread.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Positioning + Options Skew + ESI Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY is trading at 158.38, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster following the US Treasury liquidity headline. Speculative positioning remains net short JPY at -59,526, but the WoW delta of +4,107 and 4W delta of +45,712 confirm a rapid short-covering trend is underway. The options market is aggressively pricing downside protection, with 25d risk reversals at -1.93 showing a strong put skew that aligns with JPY outperformance. This positioning shift is supported by Japan's ESI of +16.5, which contrasts sharply with the persistent misses in US data (ESI -15.5). The 267bp OIS carry advantage for USD is currently insufficient to halt the JPY recovery as the Fed-BoJ policy divergence narrows. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; short-covering momentum and options skew favor further JPY strength. Catalyst: Japan National CPI report. Risk: USD/JPY holds above the SMA200 at 158.28, triggering a retail-led bounce from 74% long levels.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD has climbed to 0.7119, trading well above its SMA20/50/200 cluster as the Treasury-driven USD weakness benefits high-beta currencies. Leveraged funds are net long AUD +45,727, and while this is not yet at a 52-week extreme (pctl 75), the retail market has moved to an 86% extreme short position. This creates a classic institutional vs retail divergence, where retail traders are aggressively fading the uptrend while speculators continue to add (WoW +7,737). The 70bp carry premium for AUD via AONIA-SOFR supports the bid, provided the US liquidity shock continues to suppress USD demand. Retail capitulation risk rises if price extends toward 0.7200, potentially fueling a short-squeeze extension. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; retail extreme short provides contrarian support for trend continuation. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold priced. Risk: Broad risk-off sentiment returns, forcing an unwind of the crowded spec long.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Real Rate Support
signals.text: GBP/USD is trading at its highest level since May at 1.3599, supported by a mildly restrictive real policy rate of +0.85%. Options markets are pricing in significant uncertainty, with GBP/USD IV at 11.0% vs HV30 of 5.9%, creating a massive +5.1% volatility risk premium. This suggests the market is paying a high premium for protection despite the pair trading above its SMA20/50/200 technical cluster. The SONIA-SOFR OIS spread is nearly flat at -8bp, making the pair less of a carry play and more of a liquidity and macro divergence play following the Treasury's move. Speculative long positioning is becoming crowded (pctl 90, z +1.23), which is likely to limit immediate upside without a fresh catalyst. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD; supported by real rates and US liquidity shift, though vol premium suggests caution. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced). Risk: GBP/USD fails to hold the 1.3600 handle, triggering a profit-taking move toward SMA20 support at 1.3453.
